prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down egocentric view where the camera wearer's chest at the bottom is nearest (0.1–0.3 m), both arms extend downward and forward (0.3–0.6 m) to reach a flat green cart tray at roughly 0.6–0.8 m, and the garage floor and surrounding vehicle wheels lie further below at 1.2–2.0 m. On the tray within arm's reach, an upright white bottle on the left (frames 2–4) and a cardboard box on a lower cart to the right (frame 5, ~1.0–1.3 m away) protrude clearly toward the camera relative to the flat tray surface, while the hands rise closer to the lens in frame 2 (~0.3 m) as they unscrew the bottle cap before moving back down to the tray in frames 3–5. In frame 5, the camera wearer turns and steps slightly right, shifting the green tray to the bottom-left and revealing a lower cart with metal parts, a spare wheel on the floor to the lower-right (~1.5 m), and a second person's legs standing ~2.5 m away in the upper-right corner facing away/sideways. Compared to the cluttered RGB image, the depth map makes the vertical elevation step between the upper green tray, the adjacent lower cart, and the floor immediately obvious, as well as the upright height of the white bottle. However, the map is unreliable for thin and flat items on the tray—such as the wire brush, red screwdriver, brake pads, and thin applicator brush held in frames 3–4—which blend into the tray's depth or show blurry, bridged boundaries between the hands and the background.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates the camera wearer's torso and outstretched arms in the lower foreground (0.1–0.6 m away, within immediate reach of the tray) across all five frames, and detects the lower legs of a second person standing ~2.5 m away in the upper-right corner of frame 5. Across frames 1 to 4, the masks track the wearer's left and right arms reaching forward to the upper-left in frame 2, separating to the left and upper-right in frame 3, and converging near the center in frame 4 before shifting toward the bottom-right in frame 5 as the wearer turns right. It correctly segments the small white lubricant bottle on the left of the tray (~0.6 m away, within arm's reach) as a 'bottle' in frame 4, helping separate its round top from the cluttered background. However, the segmentation map is highly unreliable across the sequence: it fragments the wearer's single torso and two arms into multiple separate 'person' instances with hard vertical splits, and completely misses the tools, brake pads, and carts. Furthermore, it hallucinates false classes on background objects, mislabeling the blue tarp on the left as a 'person' (frames 2–3), the aerosol can on the upper-right of the tray as a 'cell phone' (frame 2), a car wheel in the upper-right background as a 'bicycle' (frame 3), and the green utility tray itself as a 'cake' (frame 5).
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks the 3D-projected finger and palm skeletons (magenta) of the camera wearer's left and right hands at roughly 0.3–0.6 m in front of and below the head, operating within 0.05–0.35 m of each other above the tray. Across the five frames, the hand skeletons show the hands close together over the center of the tray in frame 1, shifting up and left in frame 2 as the right hand arches over the left to open the bottle, separating in frame 3 (~0.35 m apart) as the right hand lifts the cap brush to the upper-right while the left rests near the center, converging again in frame 4 to coat the metal bracket, and moving down in frame 5. The skeleton wireframes clearly reveal precise finger curl, thumb opposition, and palm orientation even when the hands are partially self-occluded or visually blended against similarly toned rusty metal parts and shadows in the RGB frames. However, the pose map is unreliable in frame 5, where it completely misses the camera wearer's left hand at the bottom-left edge of the frame because the hand is partially cropped by the image boundary. It also fails to detect any yellow body skeleton for the camera wearer's torso and arms (whose shoulders and head are out of view behind the camera) or for the second person whose legs are partially visible in the upper-right corner of frame 5.
